text:
Laura: Kicking off handoff for NimbusAI reserved capacity — need quota alignment, autoscale knobs, and a short shadow load sprint. Targeting next Tue 09:00 PST for a 30m smoke. Summary + ask below.
Devon: yup, sounds good. Customer expects steady ~250 rps with bursty spikes up to ~800 for ~30s. They want probed end-to-end including auth + embeddings.
Laura: Confirmed. Our committed quota is 600 token/sec baseline for the pool. Proposal: allow burst headroom to 800 token/sec for up to 1 minute via a temporary burst pool. @Maya can you check feasibility?
Maya: Feasible. Current autoscale: step=2 nodes/min, cooldown=90s. For this tenant I can drop cooldown to 30s and pre-provision 2 burst nodes for the window. I'll open a PR for the change.
Omar: Caution: faster scaling increases p99 risk due to cold KV caches. Recommend enabling per-route tracing and a p99 latency alert at 600ms. Also enable token-level cost logging for the run.
Kai: For the shadow run I'll pin a quantized variant to keep cost down: gptq-3b-q4_0. Our eval on the customer prompt set shows negligible quality delta. I'll push the model artifact to the tenant catalog by EOD Mon.
Laura: Plan of record: 1) Quota + burst approved by Fri EOD, 2) Maya applies autoscale change + alert, 3) Kai uploads q4 model, 4) Devon runs customer-facing enablement and provides traffic template, 5) Shadow load Tue 09:00 PST (30m). Attendees: Laura, Devon, Maya, Kai, Omar.
Devon: I'll coordinate enablement and send the traffic template. Also will collect a short survey post-run to capture renewal signals and qualitative feedback.
Maya: Change PR opened: https://git.internal/r/ops/PR-4321 (autoscale cooldown -> 30s, burst_pool=2). ops-bot: autoscale change staged for tenant-nimbus.
ops-bot: autoscale change applied to tenant-nimbus (PR #4321) :white_check_mark:
Laura: Load run command for ops (k6):
```
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 30m --rps 800 ./loadtests/nimbus_shadow.js
```
Kai: We'll also run a cache prime step 10m before the run: curl https://api.redwood.ai/nimbus/prime?prefix=welcome --repeat 1000. I will upload a priming script to the repo.
Devon: Quick Q — what is the planned fallback if the q4 model shows quality regressions during the run?
Omar: Routing policy already configured: fallback -> stable-fp16. If error rate >1% or median quality drop observed, traffic will automatically route to model:stable-fp16 and we will abort burst. Region failover is enabled to us-east-1.
Laura: Ownership: post-run notes + renewal signal capture -> Devon. Ops verification and alert postmortem -> Maya. Model quality owner for eval -> Kai. I'll create the shared checklist doc and link it here.
Devon: I'll fill the checklist and post a short summary in this thread after the run :thumbsup:
Laura: Thanks all — locking schedule. Last check-in timestamp: 1823456825
